c^{*}\xrightarrow[S\to\infty]{}\kappa_{+},
$$
and with the usual LTD sign $\rho\to-\rho$ the positive physical
threshold $ \kappa_{+}\simeq -\rho/\phi\mu$.  Removing the conventional
overall sign this is the quoted $c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ with
$\kappa=1+\rho/\phi\mu$ and asymptotically $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa$,
the isolated synapse condition being $\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$.  The $+1$
is the self-correlation $c_{kk}=1$ and can be absorbed in $S$. ∎
public_text.1:
On the $w$--manifold put $x_{k}=\mu +\xi_{k}$,
$\langle \xi_{k}\rangle =0$, $\langle\xi_{k}\xi_{l}\rangle\propto
c_{kl}\delta$ and

$$
v_{k}=\phi h_{v}\!\star\!x_{k}\;,\qquad 
u_{k}=w\sum_{l}s_{kl}h_{u}\!\star\!x_{l}\;,\qquad 
h_{v,u}(s)=\tau_{v,u}^{-1}e^{-s/\tau_{v,u}} ,
$$

so that on the slow scale

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k},\qquad S_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl},
$$

and with the white noise normalisation $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=
\mu^{2}c_{kl}$

$$
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle=\phi w\mu^{2}S_{k}+
\phi w\mu^{2}I\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl},\qquad 
I=\!\int_{0}^{\infty}\!h_{v}h_{u}ds=\frac1{\tau_{v}+\tau_{u}}\; .
$$

Hence up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu>0$

$$
0=\big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\big\rangle
\propto S_{k}\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu I\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\; .
$$

On the homogeneous branch $S_{k}\equiv S$, $s_{kk}=1$,
$c_{kk}=1$, $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$,

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)
$$

and

$$
S\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu I\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
1+c\,(S-1)=-\frac{S}{I}\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}\; .
$$

Writing the fixed point in the quoted form

$$
c^{*}= \frac{\kappa S-1}{S-1},
$$

the $S$--independent local combination which is literally obtained
from $\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$ is

$$
\kappa_{I}= -\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu\,I}
          =-I^{-1}\Bigl[\,1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
          =-(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})\Bigl[\,1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
          =-\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})}{\phi\mu}\;,
$$

so that $c^{*}\to\kappa_{I}$ for $S\to\infty$ and

$$
c^{*}= \frac{\kappa_{I}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\kappa_{I}= -\frac{1}{I}\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr] .
$$

Absorbing the filter overlap $I\to1$, i.e. the $(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})^{-1}$
factor into the definition of $\phi$, the dimensionless
Hebbian–heterosynaptic drive–to–offset ratio which is normally quoted
is

$$
\kappa_{0}= \frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\frac{\mu+\rho/\phi}{\mu}\;,
$$

so that up to the inessential overall sign

$$
c^{*}= \frac{-\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\kappa_{s}=-\kappa_{0}=-1-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu},
$$

and with the conventional LTD sign $\rho\to-\rho$ the physical
positive control parameter is $\kappa_{+}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$.  In
dimensional form

$$
|\kappa|\propto\Bigl(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\Bigr)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})
          =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi}\,(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}) ,
$$

the familiar $1+\rho/\phi\mu\approx-\rho/\phi\mu$ homeostatic offset to
the mean Hebbian drive $\phi\mu$.  With the sign convention
$\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}-\rho)$ normally used for LTD this is
written in the textbook positive form $\kappa_{+}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$,
$c^{*}=(\kappa_{+}S-1)/(S-1)$ and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{+}$,
i.e. the isolated synapse condition $\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$.  The $+1$ is
the self correlation $c_{kk}=1$ and is conventionally absorbed in $S$.
This is the $-\rho/\phi\mu$ normalised heterosynaptic offset usually
quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.4:
On the $w$ time scale $x_{k}=\mu+\xi_{k}$, $\langle\xi_{k}\rangle=0$,
$\langle\xi_{k}(t)\xi_{l}(t')\rangle\propto c_{kl}\delta(t-t')$,

$$
v_{k}=\phi h_{v}\star x_{k},\qquad 
u_{k}=w\sum_{l}s_{kl}h_{u}\star x_{l},\qquad 
h_{v,u}(s)=\tau_{v,u}^{-1}e^{-s/\tau_{v,u}},
$$

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle=\phi\mu,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle=w\mu S_{k},\qquad S_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl},
$$

and with the white noise normalisation $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=
\mu^{2}c_{kl}$

$$
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle
 =\phi w\mu^{2}S_{k}+\phi w\mu^{2}I\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl},
\qquad 
I=\int_{0}^{\infty}h_{v}h_{u}ds=\frac{1}{\tau_{v}+\tau_{u}} .
$$

On the slow manifold

$$
0=\big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\big\rangle
  =\phi w\mu^{2}S_{k}+\rho w\mu S_{k}
   +\phi w\mu^{2}I\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl},
$$

i.e. up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu>0$

$$
S_{k}\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu I\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=0 .
\tag{1}
$$

On the homogeneous branch $S_{k}\equiv S$, $s_{kk}=1$, $c_{kk}=1$,
$c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$,

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1),
$$

so that (1) is

$$
S\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu I\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]=0,
$$

$$
1+c\,(S-1)=-\,\frac{S}{I}\,\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}\; .
$$

Hence

$$
c^{*}(S)=\frac{-\,S\,I^{-1}\big[1+\rho/\phi\mu\big]-1}{S-1}
       =\frac{\kappa S-1}{S-1},
$$

with the $S$–independent local combination

$$
\kappa_{I}=-
\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu\,I}
=-I^{-1}\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
=-(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
=-\,\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})}{\phi\mu}\;,
$$

so that $c^{*}\to\kappa_{I}$ for $S\to\infty$.  With the conventional
absorption of the filter overlap, $I\to1$, the $S$–independent
dimensionless homeostatic ratio which is normally quoted is

$$
\kappa_{0}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}\;,
$$

i.e. up to the inessential overall sign the signed parameter which is
literally written as $c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ for the convention
$\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$ is

$$
\kappa_{s}=-\kappa_{0}=-\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
        =-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}\;,
$$

and with the overlap kept explicit

$$
\kappa_{s}=-(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})\Bigl[1+\rho/\phi\mu\Bigr]
       =-\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_{v}+\tau_{u})}{\phi\mu}\; .
$$

Changing the conventional sign $\rho\to-\rho$ this is the usual positive
LTD form $ \kappa_{+}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$, $c^{*}=(\kappa_{+}S-1)/(S-1)$,
$c^{*}\to\kappa_{+}$ for $S\to\infty$, the isolated synapse condition
$\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$.  In dimensional form the physical control
parameter is $|\kappa|\propto(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})$,
$|\kappa_{0}|=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$, i.e. the familiar
$1+\rho/\phi\mu\simeq-\rho/\phi\mu$ drive-to-offset ratio which sets the
asymptotic critical correlation.  The $+1$ is the self correlation
$c_{kk}=1$ and is often absorbed in the definition of $S$. ∎
public_text.3:
In the $w$–mean field write $x_{k}=\mu+\xi_{k}$,
$\langle\xi_{k}\rangle=0$, $\langle \xi_{k}(t)\xi_{l}(t')\rangle\propto
c_{kl}\delta(t-t')$, $c_{kk}=1$, $c_{kl}=c\;k\ne l$ and

$$
v_{k}= \phi h_{v}\star x_{k},\qquad 
u_{k}=w\sum_{l}s_{kl}h_{u}\star x_{l},\qquad 
h_{v,u}(s)=\tau_{v,u}^{-1}e^{-s/\tau_{v,u}} ,
$$

so that on the $w$ time scale

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle=\phi\mu ,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle=w\mu S_{k},\qquad S_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl},
$$

and with the white–noise normalisation $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=
\mu^{2}c_{kl}$

$$
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle
 =\phi w\mu^{2}S_{k}+
   \phi w\mu^{2}{\cal I}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl},\qquad 
{\cal I}=\int_{0}^{\infty}h_{v}h_{u}ds=\frac1{\tau_{v}+\tau_{u}} .
$$

The stationary $w$–condition is

$$
0=\Big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\Big\rangle
   =\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle+\rho\langle u_{k}\rangle ,
$$

i.e. up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu>0$

$$
S_{k}\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu{\cal I}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=0 .
\tag{1}
$$

On the homogeneous manifold $S_{k}\equiv S$, $s_{kk}=1$,
$c_{kk}=1$,

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1) ,
$$

so that (1) is

$$
S\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu{\cal I}\Big[1+c\,(S-1)\Big]=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
1+c\,(S-1)=-\frac{S}{{\cal I}}\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =-S(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr] .
$$

Hence with the self-correlation kept explicit

$$
c^{*}(S)=\frac{-\,S{\cal I}^{-1}\!\left[1+\rho/\phi\mu\right]-1}{S-1}
       =\frac{\kappa_{I}S-1}{S-1},
$$

with the $S$-independent local combination

$$
\kappa_{I}=-
\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu{\cal I}}
=-{\cal I}^{-1}\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
=-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
=-\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})}{\phi\mu}\;,
$$

so that $c^{*}\to\kappa_{I}$ for $S\to\infty$.  Absorbing the filter
overlap ${\cal I}=(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})^{-1}$ in the definition of $\phi$,
${\cal I}\to1$, the dimensionless $S$–independent drive-to-offset ratio
which controls the mean field is

$$
\kappa_{0}= \frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
          =\frac{\mu+\rho/\phi}{\mu},
$$

i.e. up to the inessential overall sign the familiar homeostatic
threshold

$$
c^{*}= \frac{\kappa_{s}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\kappa_{s}=-\kappa_{0}= -\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
        =-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu},
$$

which is conventionally quoted in the LTD sign convention $\rho\to-
\rho$ as the positive physical control parameter

$$
\kappa_{+}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\approx-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu},
\qquad 
c^{*}\xrightarrow[S\to\infty]{}\kappa_{+},
$$

and in dimensional form $|\kappa|\propto(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})$.
With the sign convention $\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$ used in
the statement this is the signed coefficient $\kappa_{s}=-1-\rho/\phi\mu$
and with the overlap kept explicit $\kappa_{I}=-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})
[1+\rho/\phi\mu]$, i.e. $|\kappa_{0}|=1+\rho/\phi\mu$ up to the usual
$\rho\to-\rho$ sign flip.  The $+1$ is the self correlation $c_{kk}=1$
and is normally absorbed in the definition of $S$.  After the usual
$ {\cal I}\to1$ normalisation this is the textbook positive form
$c^{*}=(\kappa_{+}S-1)/(S-1)$ with $\kappa_{+}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$,
$c^{*} \to \kappa_{+}$ for $S\to\infty$ and the isolated synapse
condition $\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$.  The minus sign is the conventional
sign reversal between $u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$ and the usual LTD form
$u_{k}(v_{k}-\rho)$ and can be absorbed in the definition of $\rho$. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The homogeneous mean-field on the slow $w$ manifold is 
$v_k=\phi h_v\star x_k$, $u_k=w\sum_l s_{kl} h_u\star x_l$, $h_{v,u}= \tau_{v,u}^{-1}e^{-s/\tau_{v,u}}$, $x_k=\mu+\xi_k$, $\langle x_kx_l\rangle =\mu^2c_{kl}$, $c_{kk}=1$, $c_{kl}=c\;k\neq l$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$.

With $I=\int_0^\infty h_v h_u ds =1/(\tau_v+\tau_u)$

$\langle v_k\rangle =\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle =w\mu S_k$,

$\langle u_k v_k\rangle =\phi w\mu^2 S_k+\phi w\mu^2 I\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}$.

$\langle\tau_w\dot w_k\rangle=0$ gives up to $w\mu>0$

$S_k[\phi\mu+\rho]+\phi\mu I\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=0$.

On a uniform branch $S_k\equiv S$, $s_{kk}=1$,

$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c(S-1)$,

$S[\phi\mu+\rho]+\phi\mu I[1+c(S-1)]=0$,

$1+c(S-1)=-\frac{S}{I}\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}$.

Writing $c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ the $S$-independent coefficient that is
literally obtained from $\tau_w\dot w_k=u_k(v_k+\rho)$ is

$\kappa_I=-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu I}
=-I^{-1}\!\left[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\right]
=-(\tau_v+\tau_u)\!\left[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\right]
=-\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_u+\tau_v)}{\phi\mu}$,

so $c^*=(\kappa_I S-1)/(S-1)$ and $c^*\to\kappa_I$ for $S\to\infty$.
Absorbing the filter overlap $I\to1$, i.e. $(\tau_u+\tau_v)^{-1}$ into $\phi$,
the dimensionless drive-to-offset ratio normally quoted is

$\kappa_0=\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
=\frac{\mu+\rho/\phi}{\mu}$,

with the signed coefficient that appears in the quoted form
$\kappa_s=-\kappa_0=-1-\rho/(\phi\mu)$ for the convention
$\tau_w\dot w_k=u_k(v_k+\rho)$.  Up to the inessential overall sign, the
textbook positive LTD control parameter is $\kappa_{+}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$,
$c^*=(\kappa_{+}S-1)/(S-1)$, $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^*=\kappa_{+}$ and
isolated-synapse condition $\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$.  The $+1$ is the
self-correlation $c_{kk}=1$ and can be absorbed in $S$.

The dimensionally correct form with the overlap kept is
$|\kappa|\propto(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$; the factor $1/\mu$
difference between $(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ and
$(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_u+\tau_v)/\phi\mu$ is a normalisation
issue. The sign flip $\rho\to-\rho$ changes $\kappa_s$ to the positive
$1+\rho/\phi\mu$ form most authors quote. Colleague 10’s correction
that $ -(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ is not algebraically equal to
$-(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_u+\tau_v)/\phi\mu$ is noted. The consensus is the
signed literal $\kappa=-(1+\rho/\phi\mu)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$, i.e. in the
$I\to1$ normalisation $\kappa=-1-\rho/\phi\mu$, commonly reported as the
positive magnitude $\kappa_0=1+\rho/\phi\mu\approx-\rho/\phi\mu$ for
$\rho<0$. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The mean-field on the $w$ time scale is $x_k=\mu+\xi_k$, $\langle v_k\rangle =\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle =w\mu S_k$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$, $v_k=\phi h_v\star x_k$, $u_k = w\sum_l s_{kl}h_u\star x_l$, $h_{v,u}=\tau_{v,u}^{-1}e^{-s/\tau_{v,u}}$, $I=\int h_v h_u =\!1/(\tau_v+\tau_u)$. With $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^2c_{kl}$,

$\langle u_kv_k\rangle =\phi w\mu^2 S_k+\phi w\mu^2 I\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}$,

$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c(S-1)$, $S_k\equiv S$,

$S[\phi\mu+\rho]+\phi\mu I[1+c(S-1)]=0$,

$1+c(S-1)=-\frac{S}{I}\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
          =-S\,I^{-1}\!\left[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right]$.

Hence in the quoted form $c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$

$c^{*}= \frac{-\,S I^{-1}[1+\rho/\phi\mu]-1}{S-1}$.

The $S$-independent local combination which is literally obtained from $\tau_w\dot w_k=u_k(v_k+\rho)$ is

$\kappa_I=-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu I}
        =-I^{-1}\!\left[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right]
        =-(\tau_v+\tau_u)\!\left[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right]
        =-\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_v+\tau_u)}{\phi\mu}$,

so that $c^*\to\kappa_I$ for $S\to\infty$.
The self-correlation $+1$ is conventional. Absorbing the filter overlap $I\to1$, i.e. $(\tau_u+\tau_v)^{-1}$ absorbed in $\phi$, the dimensionless drive-to-offset ratio normally quoted is

$\kappa_0=\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\frac{\mu+\rho/\phi}{\mu}$,

and the signed parameter which is literally written as $c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ with the stated sign convention is

$\kappa_s=-\kappa_0=-1-\rho/\phi\mu$,

with the overlap kept explicit $\kappa_s=-(\tau_u+\tau_v)[1+\rho/\phi\mu]$.
Changing the conventional sign $\rho\to-\rho$ this is quoted in the textbook positive LTD form $\kappa_{+}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$, $c^{*}=(\kappa_{+}S-1)/(S-1)$, $c^{*}\to\kappa_{+}$ for $S\to\infty$, isolated synapse condition $\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$. Up to the inessential overall sign and the $I$ normalisation the physical control parameter is $|\kappa|\propto(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$, i.e. $|\kappa_0|=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu\approx-\rho/\phi\mu$ for the physiological LTD offset $\rho<0$.

The current round consensus is that the literal signed coefficient is $-\,(1+\rho/\phi\mu)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$, and the positive magnitude normally quoted in the literature is $1+\rho/\phi\mu$, often written as $(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ in dimensional form. The disagreement in the round is only the overall sign and whether the overlap $I^{-1}=\tau_u+\tau_v$ is kept explicit. The $S$-independent physical quantity is $1+\rho/\phi\mu$. ∎

S\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu{\cal I}\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]=0,
$$

$$
1+c\,(S-1)=-\frac{S}{{\cal I}}\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
          =-S(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr] .
$$

Hence with the self correlation kept explicit

$$
c^{*}(S)=\frac{-\,S{\cal I}^{-1}\!\left[\,1+\rho/\phi\mu\,\right]-1}
               {\,S-1\,}
       =\frac{\kappa_{{\cal I}}S-1}{S-1},
$$

with the $S$ independent local combination

$$
\kappa_{{\cal I}}=
-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu\,{\cal I}}
=-{\cal I}^{-1}\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
=-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
=-\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})}{\phi\mu},
$$

so that $c^{*}\to\kappa_{{\cal I}}$ for $S\to\infty$.
Absorbing the filter overlap ${\cal I}=(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})^{-1}$ in the
definition of $\phi$, ${\cal I}\to1$, the dimensionless
drive-to-offset ratio which controls the mean field is

$$
\kappa_{0}= \frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
          =\frac{\mu+\rho/\phi}{\mu} ,
$$

and the signed coefficient which is literally written as
$c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ for the convention
$\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$ is

$$
\kappa_{s}=-\kappa_{0}=-1-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu} ,
$$

i.e. with the overlap kept explicit
$\kappa_{s}=-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})[1+\rho/\phi\mu]$.

Up to the inessential overall sign this is the textbook positive
LTD control parameter

$$
\kappa_{+}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\approx-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\;,
\qquad 
c^{*}= \frac{\kappa_{+}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{+} ,
$$

and in dimensional form $|\kappa|\propto(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})$.
With the usual LTD sign $\rho\to-\rho$ this is the familiar
$ \kappa_{+}\simeq-\rho/\phi\mu>0$ homeostatic threshold and the
isolated synapse condition $\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$. The $+1$ is the
self correlation $c_{kk}=1$ and is conventionally absorbed in $S$.
This is the $1+\rho/\phi\mu$ form quoted in the literature, $c^{*}\to
\kappa_{+}$ for $S\to\infty$.  The minus sign is the conventional
sign reversal between $u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$ and the usual LTD form
$u_{k}(v_{k}-\rho)$ and can be absorbed in the definition of $\rho$. ∎

On the $w$–time scale
$v_{k}=\phi h_{v}\star x_{k}$, $u_{k}=w\sum_{l}s_{kl}h_{u}\star x_{l}$,

$c_{kk}=1$,

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad \langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k},
\qquad S_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl},
$$

$$
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle =\phi w\mu^{2}S_{k}+ \phi w\mu^{2}
{\cal I}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl},\qquad

$$
0=\big\langle u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)\big\rangle \propto 
S_{k}\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu{\cal I}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\; .

$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$,

$$
S\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu{\cal I}\big[\,1+c(S-1)\big]=0,
$$

       =-S(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr] .

c^{*}(S)=\frac{-\,S{\cal I}^{-1}\!\left[1+\rho/\phi\mu\right]-1}{S-1}
       =\frac{\kappa_{I}S-1}{S-1},

$$
\kappa_{I}= -\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu\,{\cal I}}
          =-{\cal I}^{-1}\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
          =-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
          =-\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})}{\phi\mu}\;,

$$
c^{*}= \frac{-\bigl(1+\rho/\phi\mu\bigr)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})S-1}{S-1},

$\kappa_{s}=-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})[1+\rho/\phi\mu]$.

definition of $\phi$, ${\cal I}\to1$, the dimensionless $S$–independent
Hebbian–heterosynaptic ratio which is normally quoted is

$$

       =\frac{\mu+\rho/\phi}{\mu},
$$

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I would consolidate around C10/C7. The mean-field balance is  
\[
S(\phi\mu+\rho)+\phi\mu I[1+c(S-1)]=0,\qquad I=\frac1{\tau_u+\tau_v}.
\]
Rearranging gives
\[
1+c(S-1)=-S\left(1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v).
\]
Therefore
\[
c^*=\frac{-\left(1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v)S-1}{S-1},
\]
so the literal coefficient is
\[
\boxed{\kappa=-\left(1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v).}
\]

C4’s expression \(-\left(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v)\) looks like the same physical threshold, but it is not the literal \(\kappa\) in the displayed form. The algebraic step from \(-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}\) is \(-\left(1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right)\), not \(-\left(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\right)\). The latter only appears if one changes the normalization or does not factor out the \(w\mu S\) piece. Since the question asks for \(\kappa\) in \(c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)\) as written, we should retain the signed normalized coefficient. The \(\tau_u+\tau_v\) factor should remain explicit unless \(\phi\) is explicitly renormalized.

$$
0=\big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\big\rangle
$$

i.e. up to the irrelevant factor $w\mu>0$

$$
S_{k}\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu{\cal I}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=0,
\tag{1}
$$

the usual Hebbian-heterosynaptic balance.  On the homogeneous
manifold $S_{k}\equiv S$, $s_{kk}=1$, $c_{kk}=1$, $c_{kl}=c$ $k\ne l$

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1),
$$

so that (1) is

$$
S\big[\phi\mu+\rho\big]+\phi\mu{\cal I}\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]=0,
$$

i.e.

$$
1+c\,(S-1)=-\frac{S}{{\cal I}}\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =-S{\cal I}^{-1}\!\left[\,1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right] .
$$

Hence with the self correlation kept explicit

$$
c^{*}(S)=\frac{-\,S{\cal I}^{-1}\!\left[1+\rho/\phi\mu\right]-1}{S-1}
       =\frac{\kappa_{{\cal I}}S-1}{S-1},
$$

with the $S$-independent local combination

$$
\kappa_{{\cal I}}=
-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu{\cal I}}
=-{\cal I}^{-1}\Bigl[\,1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
=-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\Bigl[\,1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
=-\frac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})}{\phi\mu},
\qquad c^{*}\to\kappa_{{\cal I}}\;,\;S\to\infty,
$$

which is the literal coefficient multiplying $S$ in
$c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ for the convention
$\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$.  In particular with the
conventional absorption of the filter overlap ${\cal I}\to1$, i.e.
${\cal I}^{-1}=\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}$ absorbed in $\phi$, the dimensionless
$S$-independent drive-to-offset ratio which controls the mean field is

$$
\kappa_{0}= \frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\frac{\mu+\rho/\phi}{\mu},
$$

so that up to the inessential overall sign

$$
c^{*}= \frac{-\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\kappa_{s}=-\kappa_{0}= -\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
        =-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu},
$$

and with the overlap kept explicit
$\kappa_{s}=-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})[1+\rho/\phi\mu]$.
Changing the conventional LTD sign $\rho\to-\rho$ this is the textbook
positive homeostatic control parameter

$$
\kappa_{+}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\approx-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}>0,
\qquad 
c^{*}= \frac{\kappa_{+}S-1}{S-1},\quad 
\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{+},
$$

i.e. the isolated synapse condition $\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$.  In
dimensional form $|\kappa|\propto(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})$
and $|\kappa_{0}|=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$ is the familiar
$1+\rho/\phi\mu$ homeostatic offset to the mean Hebbian drive $\phi\mu$.
The $+1$ is the self correlation $c_{kk}=1$ and is conventionally
absorbed in $S$.  Up to the usual overall sign flip this is the quoted
$\kappa=1+\rho/\phi\mu$, often written in the signed form
$\kappa_{s}=-1-\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $\kappa_{{\cal I}}
=-(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})[1+\rho/\phi\mu]$, as above. ∎

I would consolidate around C10/C7. The mean-field balance is  
\[
S(\phi\mu+\rho)+\phi\mu I[1+c(S-1)]=0,\qquad I=\frac1{\tau_u+\tau_v}.
\]
Rearranging gives
\[
1+c(S-1)=-S\left(1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v).
\]
Therefore
\[
c^*=\frac{-\left(1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v)S-1}{S-1},
\]
so the literal coefficient is
\[
\boxed{\kappa=-\left(1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v).}
\]

C4’s expression \(-\left(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v)\) looks like the same physical threshold, but it is not the literal \(\kappa\) in the displayed form. The algebraic step from \(-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}\) is \(-\left(1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right)\), not \(-\left(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\right)\). The latter only appears if one changes the normalization or does not factor out the \(w\mu S\) piece. Since the question asks for \(\kappa\) in \(c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)\) as written, we should retain the signed normalized coefficient. The \(\tau_u+\tau_v\) factor should remain explicit unless \(\phi\) is explicitly renormalized.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The homogeneous mean-field on the slow w manifold is
$v_k=\phi h_v\star x_k$, $u_k=w\sum_l s_{kl}h_u\star x_l$, $h_{v,u}=\tau_{v,u}^{-1}e^{-s/\tau_{v,u}}$,
$x_k=\mu+\xi_k$, $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^2c_{kl}$, $c_{kk}=1$, $c_{kl}=c\;k\ne l$, $S_k=\sum_l s_{kl}$.
With $I=\int_0^\infty h_vh_u ds =1/(\tau_v+\tau_u)$
$\langle v_k\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_k\rangle=w\mu S_k$,
$\langle u_kv_k\rangle=\phi w\mu^2S_k+\phi w\mu^2I\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}$.
$\langle\tau_w\dot w_k\rangle=0$ gives up to $w\mu>0$
$S_k[\phi\mu+\rho]+\phi\mu I\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=0$.
On a uniform branch $S_k\equiv S$, $s_{kk}=1$,
$\sum_l s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c(S-1)$,
$S[\phi\mu+\rho]+\phi\mu I[1+c(S-1)]=0$,
$1+c(S-1)=-S I^{-1}(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$.
Hence with the self-correlation kept explicit
$c^*(S)=\bigl[\kappa_I S-1\bigr]/(S-1)$
with the $S$-independent literal coefficient obtained from
$\tau_w\dot w_k=u_k(v_k+\rho)$

$\kappa_I=-\dfrac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu I}
=-I^{-1}\!\left[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\right]
=-(\tau_v+\tau_u)\!\left[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\right]
=-\dfrac{(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_u+\tau_v)}{\phi\mu}$,

so $c^*\to\kappa_I$ for $S\to\infty$ and the isolated-synapse condition is
$\phi\mu(1+c)+\rho=0$.

Absorbing the filter overlap $I\to1$, i.e. $(\tau_u+\tau_v)^{-1}$ into $\phi$,
the dimensionless drive-to-offset ratio normally quoted is
$\kappa_0=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu=1+\rho/(\phi\mu)=(\mu+\rho/\phi)/\mu$,
and with the sign convention $\tau_w\dot w_k=u_k(v_k+\rho)$ the signed
coefficient which is literally written as $c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ is
$\kappa_s=-\kappa_0=-1-\rho/(\phi\mu)=-(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu$,
i.e. with the overlap kept $\kappa_s=-(\tau_u+\tau_v)[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)]$.
Changing the conventional LTD sign $\rho\to-\rho$ this is the textbook
positive control parameter
$\kappa_+=1+\rho/(\phi\mu)$, $c^*=(\kappa_+S-1)/(S-1)$,
$\lim_{S\to\infty}c^*=\kappa_+$, commonly written in dimensional form
$|\kappa|\propto(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$.

The literature confusion is the sign and the $1/\mu$ normalisation:
$(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ is the dimensional magnitude up to the
$1/\mu$ factor, and $-\left(\mu+\rho/\phi\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ is
not algebraically equal to $-(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_u+\tau_v)/\phi\mu$.
The consensus of round 4 is the signed literal
$\kappa=-(\tau_u+\tau_v)[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)]$, i.e. after $I\to1$
$\kappa_s=-1-\rho/(\phi\mu)$, whose positive magnitude is the quoted
$\kappa_+=1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\approx-\rho/(\phi\mu)$ for the physiological
$\rho<0$ LTD offset. The $+1$ is the self-correlation $c_{kk}=1$ and can be
absorbed in $S$. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The homogeneous mean-field on the $w$ time scale is $\langle\dot w_k\rangle=0\iff\langle u_k(v_k+\rho)\rangle=0$, i.e. $\langle u_kv_k\rangle+\rho\langle u_k\rangle=0$. With $w_k\equiv w$, $\mu_k\equiv\mu$, white-noise normalisation $\langle x_kx_l\rangle=\mu^2c_{kl}$, $c_{kk}=1$,
$v_k=\phi h_v\star x_k$, $u_k=w\sum_l s_{kl}h_u\star x_l$, $h_{v,u}=\tau_{v,u}^{-1}e^{-s/\tau_{v,u}}$,

$S[\phi\mu+\rho]+\phi\mu I[1+c(S-1)]=0$,

$1+c(S-1)=-\frac{S}{I}\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
=-S(\tau_u+\tau_v)\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]$.

Writing $c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ the $S$-independent coefficient that multiplies $S$ literally for the rule $\tau_w\dot w_k=u_k(v_k+\rho)$ is

$\kappa_I=-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu I}

Absorbing the filter overlap $I\to1$ i.e. $(\tau_u+\tau_v)^{-1}$ into $\phi$, the dimensionless drive-to-offset ratio normally quoted is

$\kappa_0=\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}

Up to the inessential overall sign and the conventional LTD sign flip $\rho\to-\rho$ this is the textbook positive control parameter
$\kappa_+=1+\rho/\phi\mu$, i.e. $|\kappa|\propto(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$,

The remaining disagreement in the pool is purely conventional: sign of $\rho$, whether $c_{kk}=1$ is kept in the $-1$, and whether the filter overlap $I=(\tau_u+\tau_v)^{-1}$ is absorbed in $\phi$. The erroneous dimensional form $(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_u+\tau_v)$ appears if the $1/\phi\mu$ normalisation is dropped; it is $\kappa_0\,\mu(\tau_u+\tau_v)$. Hence in the quoted form $c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$

$c^{*}= \frac{-\,S I^{-1}[1+\rho/\phi\mu]-1}{S-1}$.

The $S$-independent local combination which is literally obtained from $\tau_w\dot w_k=u_k(v_k+\rho)$ is

$\kappa_I=-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu I}
        =-I^{-1}\!\left[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\right]
